stories.summary: How the devastated plains of Hungary were repopulated after the Ottoman wars by German Swabians, Slovaks, and Serbs, creating a colorful multinational state.

stories.title: Mária Terézia és az 1741-es pozsonyi országgyűlés
stories.summary: The dramatic moment in Pozsony when the Hungarian nobility drew their swords for Maria Theresa with the famous cry: 'Vitam et sanguinem!'

stories.title: Felvilágosult reformok: Urbárium és Ratio Educationis
stories.summary: Maria Theresa's enlightened decrees: the Urbarium limiting feudal peasant labor, and the Ratio Educationis establishing modern primary education.

stories.title: II. József, a kalapos király és rendeletei
stories.summary: Joseph II's controversial rule by decree: the progressive Edict of Tolerance, the resented German language decree, and his deathbed revocations.

stories.title: Nemzeti ébredés és a magyar nyelv mozgalma
stories.summary: How noble resistance to Germanization sparked the mother-tongue revival, György Bessenyei's writings, and the birth of modern Hungarian national identity.

stories.title: The 18th Century: Rebuilding
stories.summary: The comprehensive saga of 18th-century Hungary: repopulation, Maria Theresa's enlightened absolutism, Joseph II's decrees, and the dawn of national awakening.

stories.title: A hadba lépés tragédiája: Kassa bombázása (1941)
stories.location: Kassa főutcája és a budapesti Országház
stories.summary: On June 26, 1941, unidentified aircraft bombed the city of Kassa. Within hours, Prime Minister László Bárdossy announced in Parliament that a state of war existed between Hungary and the Soviet Union, dragging the nation into the catastrophic vortex of World War II against Teleki Pál's desperate warnings.

stories.title: A doni katasztrófa: Dermesztő pokol a Don-kanyarnál (1943)
stories.location: A Don-kanyar hófúvásai és egy alföldi falu
stories.summary: In January 1943, the Soviet Red Army launched a massive winter offensive at the Don bend. The 200,000-strong 2nd Hungarian Army, strung out along a 200-kilometer front without adequate winter clothing or heavy anti-tank weapons, was obliterated in minus 35-degree cold.

stories.title: A német megszállás és az embermentők helytállása (1944)
stories.location: Budapest, Svéd Nagykövetség és a nemzetközi gettó
stories.summary: On March 19, 1944, Hitler launched Operation Margarethe, occupying Hungary. Under the direction of Adolf Eichmann, over 430,000 rural Hungarian Jews were deported to Auschwitz within weeks. Amidst this dark abyss, brave rescuers like Raoul Wallenberg, Carl Lutz, and Sára Salkaházi risked their lives to save tens of thousands.

stories.title: A kiugrási kísérlet és a nyilas rémuralom (1944. október)
stories.location: Budapest, Magyar Rádió (Bródy Sándor utca) és a Duna-part
stories.summary: On October 15, 1944, Regent Miklós Horthy broadcast a dramatic radio proclamation announcing an armistice with the Soviet Union. However, the German SS kidnapped his son, backed an Arrow Cross fascist coup led by Ferenc Szálasi, and unleashed a reign of terror culminating in Danube bank massacres.

stories.title: Budapest ostroma és a háború vége (1944–1945)
characters: Visszatérő budapesti lakos a romok között
stories.location: A Gellért-hegy barlangjai, Lánchíd romjai és a Várnegyed
stories.summary: The Siege of Budapest was one of the deadliest urban battles of WWII, lasting 102 days. The city was pulverized, all historic Danube bridges were blown up by retreating German forces, and hundreds of thousands hid in basements. Liberation from fascism was immediately followed by Soviet occupation and deportations to forced labor camps.

stories.title: World War II in Hungary
characters: Bárdossy László és Teleki Pál miniszterelnökök
A doni katasztrófa honvédei és munkaszolgálatosai
stories.location: Kassa, a Don-kanyar, Auschwitz és Budapest
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History narrative synthesizing Hungary's tragedy in World War II: entry into the war following the bombing of Kassa, the catastrophic freezing defeat of the 2nd Army at the Don, German military occupation (March 1944) and the Holocaust, the failed October armistice attempt followed by Arrow Cross terror, and the apocalyptic 102-day Siege of Budapest.

stories.title: Mátyás megválasztása a Duna jegén
stories.summary: In January 1458, the Hungarian nobility gathered on the frozen Danube beneath Buda Castle to elect the young Matthias Corvinus, son of hero János Hunyadi, to the throne.

stories.title: A fekete sereg és a hadviselés
stories.summary: King Matthias established the legendary Black Army, one of Europe's first permanent professional standing armies, securing borders against Ottoman raids and conquering Vienna.

stories.title: A reneszánsz udvar és a Corvina
stories.summary: Under Matthias and Queen Beatrice of Aragon, the royal courts at Buda and Visegrád became Europe's foremost Renaissance centers north of the Alps, home to the famous Corvina library.

stories.title: Mátyás király és az igazságos bíráskodás
stories.summary: Known as 'Matthias the Just', the king modernized taxation through the chimney tax (füstpénz) and entered national folklore as the disguised monarch defending the common folk.

stories.title: Meghalt Mátyás, oda az igazság
stories.summary: When King Matthias died in Vienna in 1490 without a legitimate heir, Hungary entered rapid political fragmentation, crystallizing the enduring proverb 'King Matthias is dead, justice has perished.'

stories.title: Matthias Corvinus & the Renaissance Court
stories.summary: The grand historical arc of Renaissance Hungary under King Matthias Corvinus (1458–1490): his dramatic Danube election, the invincible Black Army, European Renaissance patronage and the Corvina library, the legend of 'Matthias the Just', and the national grief following his sudden death in 1490.

stories.title: A meggyengült királyság és a belső viszályok
stories.summary: Following King Matthias's death in 1490, royal central power collapsed under the Jagiellon kings. The brutal suppression of the 1514 Dózsa peasant revolt left Hungarian society deeply divided on the eve of the Ottoman invasion.

stories.title: Szulejmán szultán és Nándorfehérvár eleste
stories.summary: In 1520, the ambitious young Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent came to power in Istanbul. In 1521, the key southern stronghold Nándorfehérvár fell, leaving the Hungarian heartland completely exposed.

stories.title: A tragikus ütközet 1526. augusztus 29-én
stories.summary: On August 29, 1526, on the plains south of Mohács, King Louis II's 25,000 soldiers confronted Sultan Suleiman's 60,000-strong army. Despite a valiant cavalry assault, the Hungarian lines were pulverized by Ottoman cannons within two hours.

stories.title: II. Lajos tragédiája a Csele-patakban
stories.summary: While escaping the battlefield in the stormy dusk, the twenty-year-old King Louis II drowned in the flooded Csele brook when his armored horse stumbled, extinguishing the royal line and throwing Hungary into civil strife.

stories.title: Több is veszett Mohácsnál: A nemzeti emlékezet
stories.summary: The disaster at Mohács in 1526 ended medieval Hungarian great-power status and led to the 150-year Ottoman occupation. It permanently entered national consciousness as the supreme benchmark of tragedy and resilience.

stories.title: The Battle of Mohács (1526)
stories.summary: The catastrophic collapse of medieval Hungary at the Battle of Mohács (August 29, 1526): internal disunity after 1514, the rise of Suleiman I and fall of Nándorfehérvár, the two-hour collapse against Ottoman artillery, the drowning of King Louis II in the Csele brook, and the enduring cultural memory encapsulated in 'Több is veszett Mohácsnál'.

stories.title: A kétfejű sas és a Szent Korona
stories.summary: In Rest is History style, we explore the extraordinary bureaucratic and military machinery of the Austro-Hungarian Empire: two sovereign states under one emperor-king, three joint ministries, and a sprawling multinational army speaking a dozen languages.

stories.title: 1896: A birodalom csúcsán – A Millennium
characters: Ybl Miklós és Steindl Imre építészek
stories.summary: Budapest throws the party of the century in 1896 to celebrate the 1000th anniversary of the Hungarian Conquest. From the monumental Heroes' Square to Europe's first underground railway, the kingdom demonstrates its pride and dizzying progress to the world.

stories.title: A kávéházak és paloták városa
stories.location: Budapest, New York Kávéház, Nagykörút, Duna-part
stories.summary: How Pest, Buda and Óbuda merged to become one of the fastest-growing world metropolises. The construction of the Parliament, the sweep of the Grand Boulevard, and the rich coffeehouse culture where literature, journalism and romance flourished.

stories.title: A gőzmalmok és vasutak országa
stories.summary: Behind the glamorous coffeehouses lay industrial might: Budapest was the flour milling capital of the globe, Ganz engineering powered locomotives and European power grids, and an immense railway boom transformed the Hungarian plains into a breadbasket.

stories.title: A boldog békeidők alkonya
stories.summary: As the turn of the century arrived, the golden age of the Belle Époque began to reveal profound tensions. Rural poverty drove hundreds of thousands to emigrate to America, ethnic minorities demanded autonomy, and Europe's old order drifted toward the catastrophe of 1914.

stories.title: Austria-Hungary
characters: Andrássy Gyula és Tisza Kálmán miniszterelnökök
Mechwart András és Steindl Imre alkotók
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History narrative tracing the dual monarchy from the power-sharing compromise to the 1896 Millennium mega-celebration, Budapest's golden age of coffeehouses and heavy industry, and the poignant sunset of the Belle Époque.

stories.title: A magyar tudomány csillagai és a Nobel-díjasok
stories.summary: The remarkable contributions of Hungarian scientists and Nobel laureates to universal human knowledge, from Albert Szent-Györgyi's isolation of Vitamin C in Szeged to Katalin Karikó and Ferenc Krausz's 2023 Nobel prizes.

stories.title: A magyar találmányok és újítók világa
stories.summary: Exploring legendary Hungarian inventions that shaped modern everyday life: Ányos Jedlik's dynamo, Ignác Semmelweis's antiseptic hygiene, László Bíró's ballpoint pen, and Ernő Rubik's world-famous cube.
topics: Designation with the Essive-Modal Case: -ként and -ként tartják számon

stories.title: A magyar zenei örökség: Liszttől Bartókig és Kodályig
stories.summary: The monumental legacy of Hungarian music: Ferenc Liszt's piano romanticism, the ethnomusicological revolution of Béla Bartók and Zoltán Kodály, and the global popularity of Hungarian operetta.
topics: Cultural Contribution Valencies: Hozzájárul, gyökerezik, megalapoz

stories.title: A magyar irodalom és képzőművészet panteonja
stories.location: Nemzeti Galéria és Petőfi Irodalmi Múzeum
stories.summary: A tribute to Hungary's literary and artistic pantheon: the national poetry of Petőfi, Arany, Ady, and József Attila, alongside the visionary canvases of Mihály Munkácsy and Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka.
topics: Canonical Influence & Superlatives: Kiemelkedő alakja, legjelentősebb

stories.title: Hungarikumok, népi hagyományok és a világörökség
stories.summary: Exploring distinctive national treasures: official Hungarikums like Tokaji wine and Herend porcelain, folk traditions such as Matyó embroidery and the Mohács Busójárás, and UNESCO World Heritage landscapes.
topics: Designating National Heritage: Hungarikummá nyilvánít, védelmet élvez

stories.title: Hungarian Culture, Science & Heritage
stories.summary: A comprehensive compendium on Hungary's scientific, musical, literary, and folkloric heritage. From Nobel laureates and revolutionary inventions to classical masterpieces, UNESCO sites, and cherished Hungarikums.
topics: Designation with the Essive-Modal Case: -ként and -ként tartják számon
Cultural Contribution Valencies: Hozzájárul, gyökerezik, megalapoz
Canonical Influence & Superlatives: Kiemelkedő alakja, legjelentősebb
Designating National Heritage: Hungarikummá nyilvánít, védelmet élvez

stories.title: A magyar trikolór és nemzeti színeink története
characters: Zászlóért felelős történész a Nemzeti Múzeumban
stories.summary: Hungary's national flag is a horizontal tricolor of red, white, and green. Established during the Reform Era and codified by the 1848 revolutionary laws, its colors represent strength (red), fidelity (white), and hope (green). From the 1848 cockades to the flag with a cut-out hole in 1956, the tricolor symbolizes the nation's struggle for freedom and sovereignty.

stories.title: A Szent Korona és a koronázási jelvények misztériuma
stories.summary: The Holy Crown of Hungary is Europe's oldest surviving coronation crown. Comprising the Greek Crown (corona graeca) and the Latin Crown (corona latina), crowned with its famous tilted cross, it is not merely an ornament but the legal embodiment of Hungarian statehood through the historic Doctrine of the Holy Crown. Guarded in the Parliament with the scepter, orb, and mantle, it returned home from the US in 1978.

stories.title: Magyarország címere: a kettős kereszt és az Árpád-sávok
stories.location: Budapest, a Magyar Országos Levéltár várbeli kutatóterme
stories.summary: The Coat of Arms of Hungary is an elegant vertically split shield crowned by the Holy Crown. The right field displays the silver apostolic patriarchal cross rising from a golden coronet atop three green hills (Tátra, Mátra, Fátra). The left field features the four silver and four red stripes of the founding Árpád Dynasty, representing Hungary's rivers (Duna, Tisza, Dráva, Száva).

stories.title: A Nemzeti Himnusz: Kölcsey imája és Erkel muzsikája
characters: Szavaló diák a Szatmárcsekei emlékház udvarán
stories.location: Szatmárcseke és a Nemzeti Színház Budapesten
stories.summary: Hungary's National Anthem, 'Isten, áldd meg a magyart', is unique among world anthems: not a martial boast of military conquest, but a profound national prayer. Penned by poet Ferenc Kölcsey on January 22, 1823 in Szatmárcseke and set to immortal music by composer Ferenc Erkel in 1844, it surveys centuries of trials and blessings, asking God's protection for a people who have already suffered for past and future sins.

stories.title: A Szózat: Vörösmarty hűségfogadalma a hazához
stories.location: Székesfehérvár, a budapesti Nemzeti Színház és az Országház lépcsője
stories.summary: Regarded as Hungary's second national anthem, the Szózat ('The Appeal') was written by romantic poet Mihály Vörösmarty in 1836 and set to stirring music by Béni Egressy in 1843. Opening with the immortal imperative 'To your homeland be unwaveringly faithful', it proclaims that the soil of the motherland is the cradle and grave of every Hungarian, concluding ceremonies with an unbreakable pledge of fidelity.

stories.title: National Symbols
stories.location: Budapest, Országház és a Nemzeti Múzeum
stories.summary: A comprehensive panoramic chronicle of Hungary's sacred national symbols enshrined in the Fundamental Law. From the red-white-green tricolor representing strength, fidelity, and hope; the historic Holy Crown and coronation regalia embodying millennial statehood; the crowned coat of arms uniting the apostolic double cross and the Árpád stripes; Kölcsey's Himnusz as the collective national prayer; to Vörösmarty's Szózat as the steadfast pledge of fidelity to the motherland.

stories.title: Kossuth Lajos Amerikában és a világban
stories.summary: After the defeat of 1849, Kossuth escapes to the Ottoman Empire and embarks on a historic tour across Great Britain and America. Speaking in rich, Shakespearean English, his oratorical brilliance enchants hundreds of thousands, turning him into a global champion of liberty.

stories.title: Petőfi Sándor, a lánglelkű költő
stories.summary: Petőfi Sándor lived like a comet: passionate, uncompromising, and dedicated to the people. He wrote masterpieces on rickety tavern tables and insisted on riding to the frontline in Transylvania under General Bem, meeting a mysterious heroic death at Segesvár.

stories.title: A Nemzeti dal születése és hatalma
stories.summary: How Petőfi wrote the immortal 'Nemzeti dal' just days before March 15. The thunderous opening line 'Talpra magyar, hí a haza!' and the collective oath 'Esküszünk, esküszünk!' became the battle-cry of a whole nation that echoes across Hungarian history.

stories.title: Kokárda a szívek felett: Nemzeti jelképeink
stories.summary: The origins of Hungary's beloved national symbols: how Szendrey Júlia sewed the first tricolor cockade for Petőfi, the deep meaning of the red-white-green colors, and the debate between the Holy Crown and the republican Kossuth coat of arms.

stories.title: Március 15.: Miért ünnepel a nemzet?
stories.summary: March 15 is one of Hungary's three official national holidays and a central topic on the citizenship interview. Across cities and diaspora communities, citizens pin cockades, lay wreaths at Petőfi statues, and celebrate the birth of modern civic Hungary.

stories.title: Kossuth, Petőfi & the National Cause
stories.summary: The heroes and symbols of 1848: Kossuth's global crusade in exile, Petőfi's blazing poetry and sacrifice at Segesvár, the electric vow of the Nemzeti dal, the tricolor cockade, and the lasting meaning of March 15 in modern Hungarian civic life.

stories.title: Március 15.: A szabadság és a polgári Magyarország születése
characters: Kokárdás diák a Nemzeti Múzeum lépcsőjén
stories.location: Budapest, Pilvax kávéház és a Nemzeti Múzeum kertje
stories.summary: March 15th is Hungary's most joyous and inspiring national holiday, commemorating the 1848 Revolution. From the gathering of Petőfi and Jókai at the Pilvax Café to the printing of the 12 Points and the National Song at Landerer's press without censorship, and the sea of umbrellas outside the National Museum, March 15th marks the birth of modern civic Hungary.

stories.title: Augusztus 20.: Szent István napja és az államalapítás ünnepe
characters: Frissen felavatott honvédtiszt a Kossuth téren
Családanya a Duna-parton az esti tűzijátéknál
stories.location: Budapest, Kossuth tér, a Szent István-bazilika és a Duna-part
stories.summary: August 20th is Hungary's oldest national holiday and the official state holiday. Commemorating the 1083 canonization of King Saint Stephen and the founding of the Christian Hungarian state in the year 1000, it is celebrated with the raising of the flag and officer inauguration on Kossuth Square, the blessing of the new bread, the Saint Right procession, and evening fireworks over the Danube.

stories.title: Október 23.: A szabadságharc és a köztársaság kettős ünnepe
stories.location: Budapest, Bem tér, Corvin köz és a Parlament Kossuth tere
stories.summary: October 23rd carries double historic weight: it marks the outbreak of the heroic 1956 Revolution against Soviet tyranny and, on its 33rd anniversary in 1989, the official proclamation of the free and democratic Republic of Hungary. From the university students at the Bem statue in 1956 to the jubilant crowds at Kossuth Square in 1989, October 23rd embodies Hungary's unquenchable thirst for freedom.

stories.title: Nemzeti emléknapok: Aradi vértanúk és az Összetartozás Napja
characters: Erdélyi magyar diák a Nemzeti Összetartozás Emlékhelyénél
stories.location: Arad, a vesztőhely és a budapesti Alkotmány utca
stories.summary: Alongside the three national holidays, Hungary observes official national days of remembrance. October 6th is the National Day of Mourning for the 13 martyred generals executed in Arad and Prime Minister Count Lajos Batthyány executed in Pest in 1849. June 4th is the Day of National Cohesion, transforming the trauma of the 1920 Trianon Treaty into a celebration of cross-border unity and cultural survival.

stories.title: A diktatúrák áldozatai: Február 25. és Április 16.
stories.location: Budapest, Terror Háza Múzeum (Andrássy út 60.) és a Duna-part
stories.summary: Hungary honors the victims of 20th-century totalitarianism on two solemn remembrance days. February 25th marks the Memorial Day for Victims of Communist Dictatorships, commemorating the 1947 illegal arrest of MP Béla Kovács and the suffering of hundreds of thousands in Recsk, Gulag camps, and show trials. April 16th is the Holocaust Memorial Day, marking the 1944 ghettoization of Hungarian Jewry.

stories.title: National Holidays & Remembrance Days
stories.location: Budapest, Kossuth tér, Hősök tere és a Nemzeti Múzeum
stories.summary: A comprehensive panoramic chronicle of Hungary's three official national holidays and solemn remembrance days. From March 15th (1848 Civic Revolution, cockades, 12 Points); August 20th (King Saint Stephen, State Founding, New Bread); October 23rd (1956 Revolution and 1989 Republic); October 6th (Martyrs of Arad); June 4th (Day of National Cohesion); to February 25th and April 16th (Victims of Communism and the Holocaust). These days define Hungarian historical consciousness, identity, and civic duty.

stories.title: A helyi önkormányzatok szerepe: a közösségek önrendelkezése
stories.summary: The constitutional foundations of Hungarian local government: municipal autonomy, villages, towns, and capital districts.

stories.title: A polgármester és a képviselő-testület: a település vezetése
stories.summary: The executive leadership of the mayor, legislative function of the representative body, and administrative role of the town clerk.

stories.title: A magyar vármegyék és a területi közigazgatás
stories.location: Magyarország 19 vármegyéje és megyei jogú városai
stories.summary: Hungary's 19 counties, Saint Stephen's historical royal counties, the county assembly, and cities with county rights.

stories.title: A kormányablakok és a járási hivatalok világa
stories.summary: State territorial administration, county government offices headed by the főispán, districts, and the one-stop Citizen Windows.

stories.title: Helyi közszolgáltatások és a helyi demokrácia eszközei
stories.summary: Municipal public services (utilities, kindergartens, waste management), municipal taxes, public hearings, and local referendums.

stories.title: Local Governments & Public Administration
stories.summary: A comprehensive compendium on local self-government, municipalities, mayors, counties, Citizen Windows, and public services in Hungary.

stories.title: Hol van Magyarország?
stories.summary: Where Hungary lies in Central Europe, how the Carpathian Basin shapes its geography, and why the Hungarian language is a unique Finno-Ugric island among its neighbours.
topics: földrajzi kifejezések: elhelyezkedik, fekszik, terül el

stories.title: Megyék, folyók és városok
stories.summary: Hungary's major geographic landscapes, the Danube and Tisza river systems, Lake Balaton, the nineteen counties, and key regional cities beyond Budapest.

stories.title: A zászló és a címer
stories.summary: The deep symbolism of the Hungarian red-white-green flag, the Árpád stripes and apostolic double cross on the coat of arms, and the historical veneration of the Holy Crown.

stories.title: Magyarország szomszédai
stories.summary: Hungary's seven neighbouring states, the geopolitical landscape, the Schengen borders, and the historical Hungarian communities living across the borders.

stories.title: Első áttekintés: A honosítási beszélgetés
stories.summary: An authentic simulation of the naturalization interview where the applicant confidently presents Hungary's geography, national symbols, and borders.

stories.title: Hungary Today: Land & Symbols
stories.summary: A comprehensive synthesis of Hungary's geography, regions and rivers, national symbols and heraldry, neighbouring countries, and naturalization interview readiness.
topics: földrajzi kifejezések: elhelyezkedik, fekszik, terül el

stories.title: 1956. október 23.: A szabadság hajnala
stories.location: Budapest, Bem tér, Kossuth tér és a Bródy Sándor utca
stories.summary: On October 23, 1956, tens of thousands of university students marched in Budapest, carrying national flags with the Stalinist emblem cut out. They gathered at the Bem statue and the Parliament, demanding free elections and Soviet troop withdrawal. By nightfall, the colossal bronze Stalin monument was toppled, and the first shots were fired at the Hungarian Radio.

stories.title: A pesti srácok és a Corvin köz hősei
characters: Pongrátz Gergely, a Corvin köz legendás parancsnoka
stories.location: A Corvin mozi környéke és az Üllői út
stories.summary: Young apprentices, students, and workers—immortalized as the 'boys of Pest'—became the legendary backbone of armed resistance. Stationed at strategic intersections like the Corvin passage and Széna tér, they used homemade Molotov cocktails to destroy dozens of heavily armored Soviet tanks.

stories.title: A győzelem napjai: Nagy Imre és a semlegesség
stories.location: Budapest, Parlament és a Kilián laktanya
stories.summary: Between October 28 and November 3, Hungary tasted true freedom. Prime Minister Imre Nagy formed a democratic coalition government, dissolved the ÁVH, restored the multi-party system, and declared Hungary's perpetual neutrality, renouncing the Warsaw Pact.

stories.title: A Forgószél hadművelet és a segélykiáltás (November 4.)
characters: Nagy Imre, miniszterelnök a mikrofon előtt
stories.location: A Magyar Rádió ideiglenes stúdiója és a csepeli gyártelep
stories.summary: At dawn on November 4, 1956, Soviet forces launched Operation Whirlwind with 2,000 tanks, brutally crushing the revolution. At 5:20 AM, Imre Nagy delivered his immortal radio message to the nation and the world. Despite desperate armed resistance in Csepel and the hills, freedom was overwhelmed by brute force.

stories.title: A kádári megtorlás és a forradalom öröksége
characters: Nyugatra menekülő fiatal mérnök az osztrák határon
stories.location: A budapesti Kozma utcai börtön, az andaui híd és a Hősök tere
stories.summary: Following the defeat, the Moscow-installed puppet regime of János Kádár executed over 350 patriots—including Imre Nagy and Pál Maléter on June 16, 1958—and imprisoned tens of thousands. Over 200,000 Hungarians fled into exile. On June 16, 1989, their historic reburial sealed the collapse of communism, establishing October 23rd as the free Republic's national holiday.

stories.title: The 1956 Revolution
characters: Nagy Imre és Maléter Pál mártírok
Pongrátz Gergely és a pesti srácok
Az 1956-os emigráció és az 1989-es rendszerváltó nemzedék
stories.location: Budapest, Bem tér, Corvin köz, Országház és a Hősök tere
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History synthesis of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution: from the student outbreak on October 23rd with the flag with a hole and toppling of Stalin, to the fierce street fighting of the 'boys of Pest' at Corvin köz, Imre Nagy's declaration of neutrality, the crushing Soviet invasion on November 4th, Kádár's brutal retribution, and the triumphant moral resurrection of June 16, 1989.

stories.title: II. Rákóczi Ferenc és a Brezáni kiáltvány
stories.summary: How Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II, the wealthiest landowner in Hungary, answered the call of the peasants and launched the war of independence from Brezán Castle in 1703.

stories.title: A kurucok felkelése és hadviselése
stories.summary: The rapid spread of the Kuruc uprising, light cavalry tactics, the melancholy music of the tárogató, and the liberation of Hungarian territories from the Labanc troops.

stories.title: Az ónodi országgyűlés és a trónfosztás
stories.summary: The dramatic 1707 Diet of Ónód: declaring the dethronement of the Habsburgs, introducing taxation for nobles, copper money inflation, and the turn of military fortune at Trencsén.

stories.title: A szatmári béke és a megbékélés
stories.summary: The 1711 Peace of Szatmár: Count Sándor Károlyi negotiates an honorable compromise that preserves Hungarian constitutional rights and gives general amnesty.

stories.title: Rodostó és a nemzeti emlékezet
stories.summary: Rákóczi's dignified exile in the Turkish town of Rodostó, Kelemen Mikes's famous letters, and how Rákóczi's memory became an eternal pillar of Hungarian patriotism.

stories.title: Rákóczi's War of Independence (1703–11)
stories.summary: The complete historical saga of Rákóczi's War of Independence: from the Brezán proclamation to the Diet of Ónód, the Szatmár compromise, and the immortal exile at Rodostó.

stories.title: A szalámitaktika és a kékcédulás választások (1945–1948)
characters: Rákosi Mátyás, a kommunista párt főtitkára
stories.summary: In 1945, Hungary held free democratic elections in which the Independent Smallholders won 57% of the vote. Backed by Soviet occupation forces, Communist leader Mátyás Rákosi systematically sliced away opposing political parties one by one—a strategy he famously coined 'salami tactics'—culminating in the fraudulent blue-slip elections of 1947.

stories.title: A pártállam és Rákosi személyi kultusza
stories.location: A csepeli Rákosi Mátyás Művek és az iskolai tanterem
stories.summary: By 1949, Hungary was transformed into a totalitarian Stalinist people's republic under the new constitution. Mátyás Rákosi erected a suffocating cult of personality: giant portraits in classrooms and factories, compulsory praise in song and poetry, and total control over every aspect of private and public life.

stories.title: Az ÁVH réme: Andrássy út 60. és a recski tábor
characters: Péter Gábor, az ÁVH rettegett vezetője
stories.location: Budapest, Andrássy út 60. és a recski kőbánya
stories.summary: The cornerstone of Rákosi's totalitarian control was the ÁVH secret police, led by Gábor Péter. Operating out of Andrássy Avenue 60, midnight 'black cars' swept up citizens without trial, deporting bourgeois families to Hortobágy and political dissidents to the brutal secret quarry at Recsk.

stories.title: Koncepciós perek: Rajk László és Mindszenty bíboros
characters: Rajk László, a vádolt egykori belügyminiszter
stories.location: A Markó utcai bíróság díszterme, Budapest
stories.summary: To eliminate every potential rival and intimidate the population, Rákosi staged show trials with pre-scripted verdicts. In 1948, Cardinal József Mindszenty was drugged and sentenced to life imprisonment; in 1949, former interior minister László Rajk was executed as a fabricated 'Titoist spy'.

stories.title: Padlássöprés és a vas országa: Gazdasági zsákutca
stories.summary: Rákosi's economic dogma wreaked havoc on Hungary. In the countryside, 'sweeping the attics' robbed peasants of their last grain to force them into collective farms (téesz). In industry, the regime poured all resources into unviable heavy steel plants ('the country of iron and steel') while food shortages crippled everyday life.

stories.title: The Communist Takeover & Rákosi Era
characters: Rákosi Mátyás diktátor és Péter Gábor ÁVH-vezér
Mindszenty József bíboros és Rajk László
A diktatúra üldözöttei: parasztok, polgárok és recski rabok
stories.location: Budapest, Andrássy út 60., Recsk és az Alföld
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History synthesis of post-WWII Hungary under Stalinism: the liquidation of democracy through 'salami tactics' and fraudulent 1947 elections, Mátyás Rákosi's suffocating cult of personality and one-party state, ÁVH secret police terror at Andrássy út 60 and Recsk, fabricated show trials (Rajk, Mindszenty), and agrarian devastation through padlássöprés and heavy industrial dogma.

stories.title: Széchenyi István, a legnagyobb magyar
stories.summary: How Count István Széchenyi offered one year of his income to found the Academy of Sciences and published 'Hitel' (Credit), launching the Reform Era.

stories.title: A Lánchíd és a korszerű modernizáció
stories.summary: The construction of the Chain Bridge linking Buda and Pest, Danube river regulation, steam shipping, and breaking the nobility's ancient tax exemption.

stories.title: Kossuth Lajos és a független politikai sajtó
stories.summary: Lajos Kossuth's courageous journalism: evading Habsburg censorship with handwritten parliamentary reports, editing Pesti Hírlap, and championing serf emancipation.

stories.title: A magyar nyelv diadala és nemzeti jelképei
stories.summary: The landmark 1844 language law making Hungarian the official state language, Kölcsey's Himnusz, Vörösmarty's Szózat, and the founding of the National Theatre.

stories.title: A forradalom küszöbén: a Pilvax és a márciusi ifjak
stories.summary: The electric atmosphere on the eve of March 1848: the Védegylet, young radicals at the Pilvax café, European uprisings, and the threshold of revolution.

stories.title: The Reform Age
stories.summary: The magnificent saga of the Hungarian Reform Era: Széchenyi's foundational vision, the Chain Bridge, Kossuth's political press, the 1844 language act, and the eve of 1848.

stories.title: Az Ellenzéki Kerekasztal és a békés átmenet
characters: Antall József, az Ellenzéki Kerekasztal vezető tárgyalója

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: In September 1987, patriotic writers and dissidents met in Lakitelek, creating the Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF). By March 1989, eight democratic opposition parties and groups formed the Opposition Roundtable (EKA) to face the communist party united. At the National Roundtable talks, they negotiated the bloodless, peaceful transition from single-party rule to a multi-party constitutional democracy.

stories.title: A vasfüggöny lebontása és a határnyitás (1989)
characters: Keletnémet apa a kislányával a zugligeti templomkertben
stories.location: Hegyeshalom, a soproni határszél és a budapesti Zugliget

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: In May 1989, Hungary began physically dismantling the barbed-wire electric fence along the Austrian border. On August 19, the Pan-European Picnic near Sopron allowed hundreds of East Germans to breach the border to the West. Finally, on September 10, 1989, the Hungarian government officially opened the western border, tearing the first brick from the Berlin Wall and uniting Europe.

stories.title: Nagy Imre újratemetése (1989. június 16.)
characters: Orbán Viktor, az ellenzéki ifjúság szónoka
stories.location: Budapest, a Hősök tere és a Rákoskeresztúri új köztemető 301-es parcellája

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: On June 16, 1989, thirty-one years after the execution of Imre Nagy and the martyrs of 1956, over 300,000 Hungarians gathered at Budapest's Heroes' Square. Six coffins stood on the steps of the Műcsarnok, including an empty sixth coffin for all unknown martyrs. The dramatic speech demanding the immediate withdrawal of Soviet troops broke thirty years of silence, marking the moral funeral of the communist system.

stories.title: A Magyar Köztársaság kikiáltása (1989. október 23.)
stories.location: Budapest, a Parlament Kossuth téri erkélye és a tér

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: On October 23, 1989—the 33rd anniversary of the 1956 Revolution—provisional President of the Republic Mátyás Szűrös stepped onto the balcony of the Parliament building overlooking Kossuth Square. Before an exultant crowd of 100,000 citizens, he proclaimed the birth of the free, independent, and democratic Republic of Hungary, consigning the socialist 'People's Republic' to history.

stories.title: Az első szabad választások és az Antall-kormány (1990)
stories.location: Budapest, Országház és egy budapesti szavazóhelyiség

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: In March and April 1990, Hungarians cast their votes in the first free democratic multi-party elections in over four decades. The Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF) won a decisive victory. Historian József Antall formed a center-right coalition government, pledging to serve as 'Prime Minister of 15 million Hungarians in spirit'. The Parliament elected 1956 veteran Árpád Göncz as President, sealing the peaceful birth of the democratic third Republic.

stories.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy
stories.location: Budapest, Országház, Hősök tere és a soproni határszél

unit.title: The Regime Change: From Communism to Democracy

stories.summary: A comprehensive historical chronicle of Hungary's negotiated revolution between 1988 and 1990. From the dissident gatherings at Lakitelek and the Opposition Roundtable; the dismantling of the Iron Curtain and the border opening that helped reunify Germany; the cathartic reburial of Imre Nagy on June 16, 1989; the proclamation of the Republic on October 23, 1989; to the first free elections and the inauguration of Prime Minister József Antall and President Árpád Göncz.

stories.title: A tatárok közeledése
stories.summary: In the late 1230s, Friar Julian brought dire news from the East: the unstoppable Mongol armies were advancing toward Europe. King Béla IV attempted to prepare the kingdom and welcomed Cuman refugees, but faced deep suspicion from Hungarian nobles.

stories.title: A muhi csata
stories.summary: On 11 April 1241, the royal army clashed with Batu Khan's forces by the Sajó River at Mohi. Despite initial defense of the bridge, the Mongols outflanked the fortified wagon camp, resulting in a crushing defeat for Hungary.

stories.title: Egy elpusztult ország
stories.summary: Throughout 1241 and 1242, the Mongols laid waste to the country. After the Danube froze in winter, they crossed to Transdanubia, sacking unprotected settlements while King Béla fled all the way to Trau on the Adriatic coast.

stories.title: IV. Béla és az újjáépítés
stories.summary: In spring 1242, the Mongols unexpectedly withdrew. King Béla returned to a ruined kingdom and initiated sweeping reforms: inviting settlers, returning Cumans, and earning the historical title of 'Second Founder of the State'.

stories.title: A kővárak országa
stories.summary: The main lesson of 1241 was that wooden earthworks and open towns burned, while stone castles held out. Béla IV launched a massive fortification campaign, founding Buda Castle and building Visegrád, creating a medieval defense network.

stories.title: The Mongol Invasion (1241–42)
stories.summary: The full historical overview of the Mongol invasion of Hungary in 1241-1242: Julian's warning, the disaster at Mohi, the devastating winter of destruction, Béla IV's flight to Trau, and the king's visionary reconstruction program of stone castles.

stories.title: Buda visszavétele 1686-ban
stories.summary: In the summer of 1686, the multinational Christian army of the Holy League besieged Buda. On September 2, 1686, led by Hungarian hero Dávid Petneházy, allied troops stormed the ramparts, ending 145 years of Ottoman rule in the ancient capital.

stories.title: A győzelmes hadjáratok és a karlócai béke
stories.summary: Following Buda's fall, allied forces crushed the Ottomans at Nagyharsány (1687) and Zenta (1697) under Eugene of Savoy. The 1699 Peace of Karlowitz formally ended Ottoman occupation across virtually all of historic Hungary.

stories.title: A felszabadulás súlyos ára
stories.summary: Liberation came at immense human and material cost: scorched earth, plague epidemics, devastated towns, and crushing military taxes (porció and forspont) imposed by imperial troops quartered across Hungarian villages.

stories.title: Csalódás és elégedetlenség a felszabadulás után
stories.summary: Vienna treated Hungary as a conquered province rather than a liberated partner. The Neoacquistica Commission demanded exorbitant redemption fees from Hungarian nobles, while the Diet of 1687 revoked the hereditary right to elect kings and the right of armed resistance.

stories.title: A kuruc mozgalom és a Rákóczi-szabadságharc hajnala
stories.summary: The smoldering resentment gave birth to the Kuruc insurgent movement. When young Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II answered the call of the peasants in 1703, Hungary launched its greatest struggle for independence under the banner 'Cum Deo pro Patria et Libertate'.

stories.title: Driving Out the Ottomans
stories.summary: The dramatic liberation of Hungary from Ottoman rule (1686–1699): the heroic storming of Buda Castle on September 2, 1686 by the Holy League, crushing victories at Nagyharsány and Zenta, the milestone 1699 Peace of Karlowitz, the devastating economic toll of war on common folk, imperial absolutism and noble grievances, and the rise of the Kuruc rebellion under Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II.

stories.title: A békedelegáció Párizsban és Apponyi beszéde
stories.location: Párizs, Neuilly (Château de Madrid), Quai d'Orsay
stories.summary: In January 1920, the Hungarian peace delegation arrives in Paris, confined to the Château de Madrid in Neuilly. On January 16, Count Albert Apponyi delivers his legendary, multilingual defense of Hungary's thousand-year territorial and cultural integrity.

stories.title: 1920. június 4.: A békediktátum aláírása
stories.summary: At 16:32 on June 4, 1920, inside the Grand Trianon Palace at Versailles, two reluctant Hungarian envoys sign the treaty that dismembers the thousand-year-old kingdom. In Budapest, streetcars halt, shops close, and mourning bells toll across the grieving nation.

stories.title: Határon túli magyarság és a kisebbségi sors
stories.summary: Overnight, over three million Hungarians find themselves citizens of foreign successor states without ever leaving their homes. We explore their resilience in Transylvania, Upper Hungary, and the Vojvodina, protecting their native schools, churches, and dual identity.

stories.title: A vagonlakók és a nemzeti trauma
stories.summary: Between 1918 and 1924, nearly 400,000 refugees arrive in truncated Hungary. With housing destroyed or unavailable, entire families live in unheated freight train cars on Budapest railway sidings, fueling the deep interwar trauma and the passionate cry for revision.

stories.title: A Nemzeti Összetartozás Napja: Múltból a jövőbe
stories.location: Budapest, Kossuth tér (Nemzeti Összetartozás Emlékhelye) és Csíksomlyó
stories.summary: A century later, June 4th transforms from a day of bitter grievance into the Day of National Unity. Reflecting modern European values, the Hungarian nation celebrates cultural unity transcending borders, educational ties, and fraternal cooperation in the Carpathian Basin.

stories.title: The Treaty of Trianon (1920)
characters: Gróf Apponyi Albert és Teleki Pál
Benárd Ágost és Drasche-Lázár Alfréd aláírók
A határon túli magyarság és a mai nemzedékek
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History narrative exploring the tragedy and legacy of Trianon: Apponyi's speech in Paris, the signing at Versailles on June 4, 1920, the struggle of transborder Hungarian communities, the refugee crisis, and the modern transformation into the Day of National Unity.

stories.title: 1914: A szarajevói lövés és a háborús láz
stories.summary: In dramatic Rest is History style, we revisit June 28, 1914. Gavrilo Princip's shots in Sarajevo shatter European peace. While Vienna clamors for vengeance, Hungarian Prime Minister István Tisza initially resists the madness, before imperial momentum sweeps the nation into mobilization.

stories.title: Élet a hátországban: jegyrendszer és hadikölcsön
stories.location: Budapest, Nagykörút és a központi vásárcsarnok
stories.summary: The reality of total war strikes civilian life. As the conflict drags on into 1916, Budapest faces severe rationing, shortages of flour and coal, and propaganda urging families to empty their pockets for war bonds while women sustain the city's factories and tramways.

stories.title: Doberdó és az Isonzó pokla
stories.location: Doberdó-fennsík és az Isonzó völgye, Olasz front
stories.summary: On the brutal karst cliffs above the turquoise Isonzo River, Hungarian soldiers endure relentless artillery bombardments in the summer heat and winter ice. A poignant account of the Doberdò plateau, where hundreds of thousands sacrificed their lives.

stories.title: 1918 ősze: Az őszirózsás forradalom
stories.location: Budapest, Astoria Szálló és az Országház tér
stories.summary: October 1918 brings exhaustion and mutiny. As the front collapses, soldiers return to Budapest, ripping off imperial rosettes and pinning autumn asters to their caps. Crowds surge around Hotel Astoria, Károlyi Mihály forms a government, and Hungary declares a republic.

stories.title: A birodalom alkonya és az összeomlás
stories.summary: The euphoria of peace quickly turns to dismay. Instead of Wilsonian self-determination, foreign armies cross the demarcation lines. The historical Kingdom of Hungary fractures as Romanians, Czechs, and Serbs take control of border territories, heralding an epochal turning point.

stories.title: World War I & Collapse
characters: Tisza István és Károlyi Mihály miniszterelnökök
Ferenc József és IV. Károly uralkodók
A magyar honvédek és a hátország népe
stories.summary: A gripping Rest is History narrative sweeping through 1914 to 1918: the fatal assassination in Sarajevo, the July crisis, the bloody trenches of Doberdò, the hardships of the home front, the Aster Revolution, and the dramatic collapse of the Dual Monarchy.

stories.title: A parasztdaltól a modern koncertpódiumig
stories.summary: Bartók fused the asymmetrical rhythms and pentatonic harmonies of peasant music with radical 20th-century modernism in Bluebeard's Castle, The Miraculous Mandarin, and Cantata Profana.

stories.title: Legyen a zene mindenkié: A Kodály-módszer diadalútja
stories.summary: Zoltán Kodály transformed music education across Hungary and the world through relative solmization, hand signs, choral singing, and folk songs as a child's musical mother tongue.

stories.title: A széki táncház: Élő hagyomány a nagyváros szívében

stories.summary: Between 1950 and 1956, strict anti-abortion measures and a childlessness tax introduced under Health Minister Anna Ratkó generated a sudden baby boom whose generational waves rippled through Hungarian society for decades.

stories.title: A GYES forradalma: Otthon és munkahely között
stories.summary: Introduced in 1967, Hungary's pioneering child-care allowance (GYES) granted mothers a 3-year state-funded parental leave with guaranteed job reinstatement, fundamentally altering gender roles and maternal employment in Central Europe.
topics: Pioneering Parental Leave: The History of GYES

stories.title: Családtámogatás és lakáspolitika a mérlegen
stories.summary: Since 2010, Hungary has pursued an ambitious pro-natalist policy combining income tax allowances, prenatal loans (babaváró hitel), and housing subsidies (CSOK), generating vibrant debates over social equity and demographic efficacy.
topics: Modern Family Policies and Public Debate

stories.title: Hosszabb élet, idősödő társadalom és gondoskodás
stories.summary: As life expectancy in Hungary increases and the demographic pyramid shifts, the responsibility of elderly care falls increasingly upon the informal care economy and the 'sandwich generation', straining health institutions and family budgets.
topics: Healthcare, Longevity, and the Care Economy

stories.title: Családalapítás a 21. században: Tervek és valóság
stories.summary: Surveys reveal a persistent gap between the desired number of children and realized fertility among young Hungarians, driven by prolonged education, precarious housing, and evolving gender roles.

stories.title: A hazatérés dilemmái: Nemzetközi tapasztalat itthon
